SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Special Branch,
REPORT
File No............
Date Sept. 14, 1938.

Subject Letter entitled "A Plot to Place Incendiary Bombs in
Newspaper Offices" published in "Morning Leader" on Sept. 9.

Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. Ross.

In connection with the above letter, Zau Pang-yung
(趙邦鏻), Chinese editor of the "Morning Leader" (導報),
and Ma Ching-yuin (馬慶雲), the sender of the letter, were
interviewed at headquarters by P.A. to D.C. (Special Branch)
on September 13.

Ma Ching-yuin, who is a compositor in the employ
of the "Morning Leader", made the following statement regarding
the conversation he overheard among the coolies:-

"My name is Ma Ching-yuin, age 20, native of
Soochow. I am a compositor of the 'Morning Leader',
130 Ningpo Road, and live in the office of the paper.

"At about 8 a.m. August 24 I went to the
Bank of China, corner of Szechuen and Hankow Roads, to
make a deposit of $5. I found the offices closed.
As I did not know that the bank had been removed to another
address, I waited in the vicinity for the offices to open.
At about 8.30 a.m. I was standing beside four or five
coolies sitting by the side of Szechuen Road north of
Hankow Road outside an alleyway. One of them speaking
the Kompo dialect was telling the others about a plot of
the Huang Dao Association to set fire to newspaper
offices. They were talking quietly. I stood and
listened. When I found the offices of the Bank of
China were still closed after 9 a.m., I went to the
China and South Sea Bank to deposit my five dollars but
was told that the minimum accepted was $10. I then
returned to the office of the 'Morning Leader' and wrote
a letter to the editor reporting what I had overheard."

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER A 14 SEP. 1938 CRIME BRANCH）

主题：关于9月9日《导报》刊登的题为“在报社安放燃烧弹的阴谋”的信件。

由刑事侦缉督察罗斯（C.D.I. Ross）制作并转呈。

就上述信件一事，《导报》中文编辑赵邦鏻（Zau Pang-yung）以及该信寄件人马庆云（Ma Ching-yuin），于9月13日在总局接受了助理警司致副总监（特别支部）的问话。

马庆云系《导报》雇用的排字工人，他就其在苦力之间偷听到的谈话作出如下陈述：

“我叫马庆云，20岁，苏州人。我是宁波路130号《导报》的排字工人，住在报社办公室内。

“8月24日上午8点左右，我去四川路与汉口路转角的中国银行存入5美元。我发现银行大门紧闭。因我不知道银行已迁至他址，便在附近等候银行开门。上午8点半左右，我站在四川路北侧、汉口路以北一条弄堂外，旁边坐着四五个苦力。其中一名讲高邮（Kompo）方言的苦力正在向其他人讲述黄道会企图纵火焚烧报社的阴谋。他们低声交谈。我站着旁听。发现过了上午9点中国银行仍未开门后，我便去中南银行存那5美元，但被告知最低存款额为10美元。随后我回到《导报》办公室，写了一封信给编辑，报告我所偷听到的内容。”

（印章：副总监 A 1938年9月14日 罪案科）

September 9, 1938. Morning Translation.

Morning Leader publishes the following letter :-

A PLOT TO PLACE INCENDIARY BOMBS IN NEWSPAPER OFFICES

To the Editor :
Relying on Japanese influence, traitor Zang Nyoh-tsing (曾仲鳴) is openly selling his country. He organized a Huang Dao Association to induce ignorant Chinese and wicked loafers to assassinate patriotic youths and anti-Japanese elements.
Recently the Huang Dao Association held a secret meeting to discuss drastic measures to deal with Chinese newspapers published under foreign protection. It was proposed to bribe news vendors to place small incendiary bombs in newspaper offices. The bomb has a spring device which sets off the bomb after about 20 minutes. The explosion would immediately send flames up through the roof. I heard a number of barefooted coolies sitting by the side of -- Road discussing the plot.
The S.M.C. has already issued a circular order for the arrest of Zang Nyoh-tsing, but the lawless elements are continuing to disturb peace and order in the Settlement in an attempt to exterminate patriotic elements. Tens of terrorist cases are occurring each month simply because "--"wishes to seize all the rights in the Settlement.
In my opinion, the following measures should be adopted against the plots of the Huang Dao Associations:-
(1) The S.M.C. should be requested to arrest the committeemen of the Huang Dao Association.
(2) All persons who have relatives or friends serving as committeemen of the Huang Dao Association should sever all connection with such relatives and friends; they should not allow themselves to be bribed.
From a reader.
(Editor's notes:- As the information contained in the above letter is based on gossip among some coolies, it may not be reliable. The suggestion that all persons sever connection with committeemen of the Huang Dao Association merits support. Chinese in Shanghai should not have anything to do with Japanese and traitors.)

Standard :-

ZAU HAU-SUNG NOT GOING TO HONGKONG

On the night of September 7, our reporter interviewed Mr. Zau Hau-sung (周佛海) at his home. Mr. Zau declared that the reports about his movements were all incorrect. On September 7 he received an anonymous letter of warning to which he published a reply in the newspapers in order to remove the misunderstanding. Mr. Zau added that he had cancelled his trip to Hongkong in company with Chen Tao-yi (陳陶遺), former Governor of Kiangsu Province.

1938年9月9日。晨间译稿。

《导报》刊登如下信件：

在报社安放燃烧弹的阴谋

致编辑：
汉奸曾仲鸣（Zang Nyoh-tsing）倚仗日本势力，公然卖国。他组织了一个黄道会，诱骗无知华人和邪恶懒汉刺杀爱国青年及抗日分子。
近日，黄道会举行秘密会议，讨论对付在外商保护下出版的中国报纸的严厉措施。有人提议贿赂报贩，在报社内安放小型燃烧弹。该炸弹装有弹簧装置，可在约20分钟后引爆。爆炸将立即使火焰冲穿屋顶。我听到数名赤脚苦力坐在--路旁讨论此阴谋。
工部局已发布通缉令逮捕曾仲鸣，但不法之徒仍继续扰乱租界内的和平与秩序，企图消灭爱国分子。每月发生数十起恐怖案件，仅仅因为“--”企图攫取租界内的一切权利。
笔者认为，针对黄道会的阴谋应采取以下措施：
(1) 应要求工部局逮捕黄道会委员。
(2) 所有亲属或朋友担任黄道会委员的人，应与这些亲友断绝一切联系；不应受其贿赂。
读者来信。
（编者按：由于上述信件所载信息基于某些苦力间的流言，可能不可靠。建议所有人与黄道会委员断绝联系的观点值得支持。上海华人不应与日本人及汉奸有任何瓜葛。）

标准报：

周佛海不去香港

9月7日晚，本报记者在其家中采访了周佛海（Zau Hau-sung）先生。周先生声明，有关其行踪的报道均不正确。9月7日，他收到一封匿名警告信，为此他在报纸上发表了回复以消除误解。周先生补充说，他已取消与前江苏省省长陈陶遗（Chen Tao-yi）一同前往香港的行程。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
SEP 1 3 1938
Burning of Press
Building Fails
Two Chinese Sentenced for
Plotting ; Member of Bomb
Throwing Party Arrested

Two Chinese, who admitted that
they plotted to bomb or burn the
Chinese-language newspaper "Morn-
ing Leader" on behalf of a Japanese
named Shiotani and the so-called
"Economic Rehabilitation Society,"
were sentenced to fifteen years in
prison each yesterday in the First
Special District Court, where they
appeared on remand, charged with
instigating arson. The "Economic
Rehabilitation Society" is a Japanese-
sponsored organization with head-
quarters in Brenan Road, according
to testimony.
Besides the "Morning Leader,"
which is published by the British-
owned University Press at 130 Ning-
po Road, the accused are said to have
conspired to fire three other foreign-
registered Chinese papers in the In-
ternational Settlement and French
Concession. The publishing of alleged
anti-Japanese articles in these journ-
als, it is held, provided the under-
lying motive for the contemplated
acts of terrorism.
The plot involving the "Morning
Leader" was to have been realized
during the emergency period at the
middle of last month. Mr. J. A. E.
Bates, the publisher, however, learned
of in time to prevent it from being
carried out.

Conferences with Japanese

The two prisoners, Hsia Wei-sun
and Kao Yung-chang, were arrested
after Hsia had unsuccessfully tried to
bribe an employee of the University
Press to place a timed fire-producing
device in the printing-room of the
establishment. It was testified yester-
day that Hsia met this employee,
Tsang Ping-yen, in lodging-houses and
the Oriental Hotel (Sincere's Build-
ing) to talk over the scheme. In the
Oriental Hotel, it was admitted, a
Japanese named Shiotani participated
in the conferences, with Kao Yung-
chang acting as interpreter. Shiotani
asked for detailed information regard-
ing the University Press building.
Tsang was to get $200 for joining the
conspiracy and an additional $400
when the "bomb" had been pro-
duced and set off. He was further
to get privileges in Hongkew, and a
job.
Tsang informed Mr. Bates about the
plan, and the Police were called in.
Hsia was first arrested, in Kaifeng
Road, and later Kao was seized.
Mr. T. S. Lea, Assistant Municipal
Advocate, presented the case for the
Police at yesterday's and last week's
hearings.

Bomb Party Member Arrested

Alleged to have been a member of
the party of three men who, on May
21 at 10 p.m., threw a bomb at the
offices of the "Morning Leader,"
Hongkong registered Chinese lang-
uage newspaper, at 130 Ningpo Road,
a 26-years-old native of Kompo of the
coolie class was arrested by the
Settlement Police yesterday.
As a result of the bomb throwing
five Chinese were injured, including a
Chinese constable of the Shanghai
Municipal Police. The perpetrators
of the act made their escape. The
other two members of the party are
still at large.
The Economic Rehabilitation So-
ciety has been identified by the police
as being no other than the "Huang
Tao Hui" or Yellow Way Society
which has been responsible for
numerous acts of terrorism in the
French Concession and Settlement
during the past six months.

《字林西报》，
1938年9月13日
焚烧报业大楼未遂
两名中国人因策划阴谋被判刑；投掷炸弹团伙成员被捕

两名中国人承认，他们代表一名名为盐谷（Shiotani）的日本人和所谓的“经济复兴社”，策划轰炸或焚烧中文报纸《导报》，昨日在第一特区地方法院各被判处十五年监禁。他们在还押候审期间出庭，被控煽动纵火。据证词称，“经济复兴社”是一个由日本赞助的组织，总部设在白伦路（Brenan Road）。
据称，除了由英商大学书局（University Press）在宁波路130号出版的《导报》外，被告还密谋在国际租界和法租界纵火焚烧另外三家在外注册的中国报纸。据认为，在这些报刊上发表所谓的反日文章，是预谋实施恐怖行为的根本动机。
涉及《导报》的阴谋原定于上月紧急状态期间实施。然而，出版人J. A. E. Bates先生及时获悉，阻止了阴谋的实施。

与日本人的会谈

两名囚犯夏维松（Hsia Wei-sun）和高永昌（Kao Yung-chang）是在夏试图贿赂大学书局的一名员工在印刷车间安放定时发火装置未果后被捕的。昨日作证称，夏在旅馆和东方饭店（先施公司大楼）与该员工臧炳炎（Tsang Ping-yen）会面，商讨该计划。据承认，在东方饭店，一名名为盐谷（Shiotani）的日本人参与了会谈，由高永昌担任翻译。盐谷询问了有关大学书局大楼的详细信息。臧加入阴谋可获得200美元，并在“炸弹”制造并引爆后再获400美元。他还将在虹口获得特权和一份工作。
臧将计划告知了Bates先生，警方随即介入。夏首先在开封路被捕，随后高也被抓获。
助理市检察官T. S. Lea先生在昨日及上周的听证会上代表警方陈述案情。

炸弹团伙成员被捕

据称是一名三人团伙的成员，该团伙于5月21日晚上10点向位于宁波路130号的香港注册中文报纸《导报》办公室投掷了一枚炸弹，这名26岁的高邮籍苦力阶层男子昨日被租界警察逮捕。
此次投掷炸弹导致五名中国人受伤，其中包括一名上海公共租界工部局警务处的华捕。作案者逃脱。该团伙的另外两名成员仍在逃。
警方已确认，“经济复兴社”即为“黄道会”，该会在过去六个月中应对法租界和公共租界内的多起恐怖行为负责。

Au Wei Sung
Shanghai
Central 29/8/38 ///// Clerk Sung
translated

Au Wei Sung, alias Ching Lei, age 30, native of Shanghai,
employed as an accountant and residing at the Hwa Tung
Printing Co. (Epoch Evening Post), 169 Avenue Rd.

At the beginning of June 1938, one named Sung (A customer
of the aforesaid printing office), employed by the "Shanghai
Daily News Mosquito Newspaper Co." introduced me to one named
Kau Kuo Shing, chairman of "Shanghai Workers Unions' Corporation"
(The organization of this group of unions has not as yet been
made public) who urged me to form a Printers' Union, and I
agreed to do so.

After a few days the so-called "Shanghai Workers Unions'
Corporation" held a meeting, at which representatives of all
businesses were expected to attend. I attended the conference
as a representative of the Printers Union.

During the conference I became acquainted with a Japanese
and his interpreter named Kau Yoong Tsong (2nd accused). The
Japanese attended for the purpose of giving aid and opinion
regarding the formation of Workers Unions, as they were interested
in the organisation.

After the lapse of about one month I received a telephone
call from the said interpreter Kau asking if I had friends
employed in the University Press Ltd. I replied in the affirmative
and when I asked him the reason for the inquiry he requested
me to bring my friend employed by the University Press to his
home, situated at the Chaoufoong Alleyway, Brenan Rd. I did not
give my consent.

After two or three days I had a further telephone call
page_data.zh:
夏伟生
上海
中央 1938年8月29日 ///// 书记员 Sung
译文

夏伟生，别名程雷（Ching Lei），30岁，上海人，受雇为会计师，居住在爱文义路169号华通印刷公司（《文汇报》）。

1938年6月初，一名名为宋（Sung）的人（上述印刷厂的客户），受雇于“上海每日新闻蚊报公司”（Shanghai Daily News Mosquito Newspaper Co.），将我介绍给名为高国兴（Kau Kuo Shing）的人，他是“上海工会联合会”（Shanghai Workers Unions' Corporation）的主席（该工会组织的性质尚未公开），他敦促我组建一个印刷工人工会，我同意了。

几天后，所谓的“上海工会联合会”召开了一次会议，预计各行业的代表都将出席。我作为印刷工会的代表参加了会议。

在会议期间，我结识了一名日本人及其翻译高永昌（第二被告）。日本人出席的目的是就工会的组建提供援助和意见，因为他们对该组织感兴趣。

大约一个月后，我接到上述翻译高的电话，询问我是否有朋友在商务印书馆有限公司工作。我给予了肯定的回答，当我询问他查询的原因时，他要求我将我在商务印书馆工作的朋友带到他位于倍开尔路朝丰里（Chaoufoong Alleyway）的家中。我没有同意。

两三天后，我又接到一个电话

page_data.en:
Page 2
from the interpreter Kau,who requested my attendance at his
home. When I called at his home he asked me if my friend
employed by the University Press attended. I again enquired
the reason why he wanted to meet my friend,and then Kau stated
that the topics or head lines on the University Press
newspapers were always grossly exaggerated beyond fact. My
friend would be entreated,he went on to say,to teach the
management of the University Press a lesson. When I inquired
as to what measures it was proposed to adopt Kau stated "
An explosive substance". He added,if the deed was performed
the sum of $500 would be bestowed as remuneration. I promised
him to inform my friend regarding the affair.
On the following day I booked a room at the Loong Ziang
Lodging House, Avenue Rd. and consulted one named Tsong Ping
Yee,employed at the Paper Section of the University Press Ltd.
As the project was detrimental to morality,he expressed his
unwillingness. However,in order to make money on this matter
(Their money was squeezed from our Chinese people) we finally
decided to seize this opportunity and to keep in contact with
with the Japanese and his interpreter. After arrangement by
telephone,Kau Yoong Tsong,together with the Japanese,attended
the room at the Oriental Hotel,which apartment I rented,Tsong
Ping Yee was also present. Inside the apartment we four persons
held a conference and a demand for payment of $500 for the
execution of the proposed incendierism was made to the Japanese.
This demand was however accepted on the condition that Tsong
Ping Yee should produce two copies of his photograph,but this
page_data.zh:
第2页
来自翻译高，他要求我去他家。当我到他家时，他问我在商务印书馆工作的朋友是否来了。我再次询问他想见我朋友的原因，然后高表示，商务印书馆报纸上的话题或标题总是严重夸大，不符事实。他接着说，将恳求我的朋友教训一下商务印书馆的管理层。当我询问打算采取什么措施时，高表示“一种爆炸性物质”。他补充说，如果事情做成，将给予500美元作为报酬。我答应他会将此事告知我的朋友。
第二天，我在爱文义路的龙翔旅馆（Loong Ziang Lodging House）订了一个房间，并与在商务印书馆有限公司纸品部工作的章炳義进行了商议。由于该项目有违道德，他表示不愿意。然而，为了在这件事上赚钱（他们的钱是从我们中国人身上榨取的），我们最终决定抓住这个机会，并与日本人及其翻译保持联系。经过电话安排，高永昌与日本人一起出席了我租下的东方饭店的房间，章炳義也在场。在房间内，我们四人举行了会议，并向日本人提出了执行拟议纵火案需支付500美元的要求。然而，这一要求被接受的条件是章炳義需提供两张他的照片，但这

page_data.en:
Page 3
request I rejected. When mention was made about the payment
of the money, the interpreter Kau stated that the payment of
the sum of $200 would be made in advance, as soon as the
required photographs were handed in, the remaining $400 being
paid after perpetration of the arson project. Then we all departed
without result.
After their departure, I consulted with Tsong Ping Yee
concerning the installment payment, as we wished to obtain the
full payment prior to the work, and we finally decided to put
the matter aside.
After the lapse of about twenty days Kau Yoong Tsong again
telephoned to me inquiring about the affair. He appeared to be
eager regarding the business and I thought that our scheme
might receive some profit. I, therefore, immediately tried to
locate Tsong Ping Yee, but failed. When I tried to find him on
the second occasion I visited his home where I was taken into
custody by detectives.
The above is true.
Cross-marked and Signed.
J. Ross
7/9/8/38

第3页
我拒绝了该请求。当提及付款事宜时，翻译高（Kau）表示，一旦提交所需的照片，将预付200美元，余下的400美元将在纵火项目实施后支付。随后我们所有人无果而散。

他们离开后，我与宗平义（Tsong Ping Yee，音译）就分期付款一事进行了商议，因为我们希望在工作开始前获得全额付款，最终我们决定将此事项搁置。

大约二十天后，高永宗（Kau Yoong Tsong，音译）再次致电给我，询问此事。他似乎对这笔生意很急切，我认为我们的计划可能会带来一些收益。因此，我立即试图寻找宗平义，但未能找到。当我第二次试图寻找他时，我前往他的住所，在那里我被侦探拘捕。

以上属实。

At about 9p.m/ 17/6/39 an urgent telephone call was received at Central Station from Honan Road Police Telephone Box requesting immediate Police assistance. The sound of Police whistle being blown was also heard through the telephone receiver.

The Station alarm was rung by S.I. Watson, Charge Room Officer, and a strong detachment of uniformed and C.I.D. personnel under D.S.I. Gazeley and S.I. Biggs attended.

Upon arrival at Honan and Ningpo Roads intersection a large crowd had congregated, therefore a cordon of Police were immediately deployed around the vicinity extending from the Police Box Honan Road to Lane 120, Ningpo Road.

Immediately upon arrival of the Police party, C.P.C. 2596, minus uniform jacket cap and belt, but carrying a loaded pistol in his hand, reported to D.S.I. Gazeley that a number of armed men had entered the rear door (located inside Lane 120 Ningpo Road) of the University Press, No.130 Ningpo Road, and that he, after having telephoned the station for immediate assistance from Honan Road telephone box, had entered the rear door of the China Equitable Bank, No.144, Ningpo Road rushed to the front of the premises and had fired two shots from his service pistol (No.3259) through the green sun blind at some men whom he saw running away from the scene.

C.P.C. 2590, Meu Tsoong Tsong reports:-

Between 7p.m. and 11p.m. 17/6/39 I was detailed for
duty in front of the "Morning Leader" Newspaper Office,
130 Ningpo Road.
At about 8.50p.m. even date a male Chinese age about
30, height about 5'2/3", medium build, red round face,
wearing black jacket and grey pants, speaking Kompo dialect
approached me and stated that he had come to investigate into
some affairs and warned me to keep quiet and, at the same time
drew a Mauser pistol in his hand and pointed it at me.
Suspecting that he was an undesirable character I ran to the
adjoining alleyway (Shing Zung Lee) where I used a telephone
box and reported the matter to the station. The man did not
follow me. When I closed the door of the telephone box I
observed that the rear door of one of the houses in the lane
was open (Chung Woo Bank). I then entered this house with a
view to leave via the front door, however the front door had
already been closed. At this juncture I suddenly heard the
sound of shooting 4 or 5 times, whereupon I climbed up the
door and looked through a window when I saw a man, description
unavailable, escaping East to West along Ningpo Road. Knowing
that he was an accomplice I immediately fired two shots at him
but I did not know whether or not they were effective. After
which I then left the house via the rear door and chased behind
him and at the same time I took off my uniform with a view to
avoiding being easily recognized. I blew my whistle and ran
South along Honan Road towards Ningpo Road but I failed to
trace him. In the meantime foreign and Chinese police officers
arrived at the place and, in the presence of D.S.I. Gasley I
reconstructed what had happened.
Sgd Meu Tsoong Tsong.

华籍巡捕2590号，梅宗宗（Meu Tsoong Tsong）报告：-

1939年6月17日晚7时至11时之间，我被指派在宁波路130号《晨报》（Morning Leader）报社门前执勤。
同日约晚上8点50分，一名中国男子，年龄约30岁，身高约5英尺2/3英寸，中等身材，红圆脸，身穿黑色夹克和灰色裤子，讲宁波话，走近我，声称他是来调查一些事务的，并警告我保持安静，同时从手中掏出一支毛瑟手枪指着我。怀疑他是一个不良分子，我跑进相邻的弄堂（兴宗里 Shing Zung Lee），使用电话亭向巡捕房报告了此事。该男子没有跟随我。当我关上电话亭的门时，我观察到弄堂内一户人家（中汇银行 Chung Woo Bank）的后门是开着的。于是我进入这所房子，打算从前门离开，然而前门已经关闭。就在这时，我突然听到四五声枪响，于是我爬上门口，透过窗户看到一名男子，外貌描述不详，沿宁波路从东向西逃跑。知道他是同伙，我立即向他开了两枪，但我不知道是否击中。之后，我从后门离开房子，在他后面追赶，同时我脱下制服，以避免被轻易认出。我吹响哨子，沿河南路向南朝宁波路方向跑去，但未能追踪到他。与此同时，外籍和华籍警官到达现场，在分区副督察 Gasley 面前，我重现了当时发生的情况。

lay down on the floor and then heard two more pistol shots fired.
After the situation had calmed I stood up and found that the
two armed men had already gone. The above is my true statement.

Signed.

1939年6月17日晚约8时50分，当我坐在一名名叫蒋宗廷（Tsiang Tson Tin）的雇员对面处理公务时，我突然听到两声枪响。当我转过头时，我看到两名男子正用手枪向我射击。我立刻趴在地上，随后又听到两声枪响。局势平息后，我站起身，发现两名持枪男子已经离去。以上是我的真实陈述。

Lee Ming Jing,
Peiping.                      xx self.
                               translated
Central Stn.      17-6-39      /--------    Clerk Fan

Lee Ming Jing, aged 50 years, native of Peiping, employed as
a watchman and residing in the Morning Leader Newspaper Office,
130 Ningpo Road. I have been detailed for watching the rear door
of the above newspaper office. At about 8.50p.m. 17-6-39, whilst
chatting with the night duty watchman named Daung Yue Sung at the
rear door of the above address, there appeared four male Chinese,
two dressed in foreign style clothes and two wearing Chinese
clothes, who entered the rear door. Due to the fact that my
eyesight is poor, I could not see clearly the colour of the
clothes worn by these men nor could I perceive their figures.
At the time of entering the rear door, they asked us whether one
named Loh was in. I replied in the negative. At this juncture,
they, 4 in number, rushed to the office. We following them with
intent to stop them going further, but it was impossible and
they fired shots from their pistols into the office. I could
not ascertain who were the persons responsible for the shooting.
During the crisis, I immediately retreated and entered the
dormitory inside the rear door. About 5 or 6 minutes later,
following four or five pistol reports, I emerged from the
dormitory when the squad of Police arrived and commenced to
investigate the case. I have no knowledge as to which direction
the persons responsible for the shooting affray escaped. The
above is my true statement.

                               Signed.

李明镜（Lee Ming Jing），
北平。                      xx 自述
                               翻译
中央巡捕房      1939年6月17日      /--------    书记员 Fan

李明镜（Lee Ming Jing），50岁，北平人，受雇为更夫，居住在宁波路130号《导报》馆。我被指派看守上述报馆的后门。1939年6月17日晚约8时50分，当我和名为唐岳松（Daung Yue Sung）的夜班更夫在上述地址的后门聊天时，出现了四名中国男子，其中两人身穿西式服装，两人身穿中式服装，他们进入了后门。由于我视力不佳，我看不清这些人所穿衣服的颜色，也看不清他们的体型。在进入后门时，他们询问是否有一位姓罗的人在。我回答不在。此时，这四个人冲向办公室。我们跟随他们意图阻止他们进一步行动，但未能成功，他们用手枪向办公室内开枪。我无法确定是谁开的枪。在危急时刻，我立即撤退，进入后门内的宿舍。大约五六分钟后，在听到四五声枪响后，我从宿舍出来，此时警察小队抵达并开始调查此案。我不知道开枪肇事者向哪个方向逃跑了。以上是我的真实陈述。

                               签名。

page_data.en:
Daung Yeu Sung, age 32, M/teaboy employed and
residing at the Morning Leader Office.
Changchow.
Central Stn.        17-6-39.

    At about 8.50p.m. 17/6/39 whilst I was standing together
with another teaboy named Lee Ming Jing at the rear door of
the above premises (leading to Lane 120 Ningpo Road), four
male Chinese suddenly pushed open the door, which was closed
but not bolted, and entered. Two of them produced Mauser
pistols and intimidated us and one of them then kept guard
at the foot of the stairway whilst the other two men rushed
straight into the office.premises. One of the men asked me
who was the man named Loh. I then heard the sound of pistol
shots coming from the office. I immediately hid myself in a
room near to the rear door. After firing 4 or 5 shots the
men decamped at the point of entry. I also heard the sound
of police whistle being blown. Later police officers arrived
and brought me to Paulun Hospital to identify any of the
wounded persons detained there. I was failed to identify
either of the 3 men as being concerned in the shooting on
Ningpo Road. This is my true statement.
                                Sgd. Daung Yeu Sung.

Description of culprits:-
(1) Age about 25, height 5'7", slim build, long face, black
long hair brushed backwards, wearing dark grey foreign style
suit, Shanghai dialect. ARMED.
(2) Age about 26, height 5'5", slim build, long pale face,
long hair parted in the centre, wearing grey foreign style
suit. ARMED.
(3) Age about 30, height 5'6", wearing grey long gown.
(4) Age about 27-8, height 5'5", wearing bluish-grey long gown.

唐岳松（Daung Yeu Sung），32岁，男，茶役，受雇并居住在《导报》馆。
常州。
中央巡捕房        1939年6月17日。

    1939年6月17日晚约8时50分，当我和另一名茶役李明镜（Lee Ming Jing）一起站在上述处所（通往宁波路120弄）的后门时，四名中国男子突然推开了虽关闭但未上闩的门并进入。其中两人掏出毛瑟手枪恐吓我们，其中一人在楼梯口把守，另外两人则直接冲进办公室。其中一人问我谁姓罗。随后我听到办公室传来枪声。我立即躲藏在靠近后门的一个房间里。在开了四五枪后，这些人从来时的入口逃窜。我还听到了吹警笛的声音。后来警官抵达，并将我带到宝隆医院（Paulun Hospital）去辨认那里拘留的任何伤者。我未能辨认出三名男子中有任何一人涉及宁波路的枪击案。这是我的真实陈述。
                                签名：唐岳松（Daung Yeu Sung）。

Sung Nyih Tser, C.P.W. 23, native of Shantung, M/residing
at 9 Dah Kwei Lee, Connaught Road, states as follows:-
Between 4p.m. and 12m.n. on the 17-6-39 I was detailed for
duty at Lane 120 off Ningpo Road.
At about 8.50p.m. same date, whilst sitting inside the
mouth of the alleyway, I was approached by a male Chinese,
dressed in grey foreign style clothes, age about 30, height 5'7"
stout build, round face, sallow complexion, who asked me where
the rear entrance of The Morning Leader Newspaper Office was.
I indicated the way to him by pointing my finger at the rear
door of the said concern. At this juncture, another male
Chinese, age about 30, height 5'3", medium build, round face,
fresh complexion, wearing black cotton jacket and pants,
speaking Kompo dialect approached and intimidated me with a
mauser pistol instructing me to acknowledge the situation and
not to move. Meanwhile I heard pistol reports proceeding from
outside the alleyway and the sound of breaking glass. After
the firing was over, the man who kept guard upon my person ran
away and was quite beyond pursuit when I emerged from the
alleyway. The above is my true statement.

Signed.

宋义泽（Sung Nyih Tser），华捕警号 23，山东人，男，居住在康纳脱路大贵里9号，陈述如下：-
1939年6月17日下午4时至午夜12时之间，我被派往宁波路120弄执行勤务。
同日约晚上8时50分，当我坐在巷口内时，一名身穿灰色西式服装、年龄约30岁、身高5英尺7英寸、体格健壮、圆脸、面色蜡黄的中国男子走近我，询问《导报》馆的后门在哪里。我用手指向该机构的后门为他指路。此时，另一名年龄约30岁、身高5英尺3英寸、中等身材、圆脸、面色红润、身穿黑色棉布夹克和长裤、讲广东话的中国男子走近，用一把毛瑟手枪恐吓我，命令我识相点，不许动。与此同时，我听到巷外传来枪声和玻璃破碎的声音。枪击结束后，负责看守我的那名男子逃跑了，当我走出巷子时，他已远远超出追捕范围。以上是我的真实陈述。

签名。

page_data.en:
Mo Sieu Sai, age 55, M/C.P.W. 606, 283 Shanghai-
Shantung.                                                                 kwan Road.

I was on duty at the first alleyway of Lane 120 Ningpo
Road between 2p.m. and 10p.m. 17/6/39.
At 8.50p.m. even date I suddenly heard a sound of shooting
coming from outside the lane. I immediately took my pistol
in hand and proceeded outside when I encountered C.P.C.2596,
who also held his pistol in his hand and running into the lane
stated that we must telephone to the station immediately.
I then closed the iron gates of the lane but I did not see
the man who fired the pistol. Later, police officers came
and ordered me to open the gates.
The above is my true statement.

Sgd. Mo Sieu Sai.
page_data.zh:
莫少赛（Mo Sieu Sai），55岁，男，华捕警号 606，上海昆山路283号。
山东。                                                                 

1939年6月17日下午2时至晚上10时，我在宁波路120弄的第一条支弄执勤。
同日晚上8时50分，我突然听到弄堂外传来枪声。我立即拿起手枪走到外面，遇到了同样手持手枪跑进弄堂的华捕警号2596，他说我们必须立即打电话回巡捕房。随后我关上了弄堂的铁门，但我没有看到开枪的人。后来，警官到来并命令我打开大门。
以上是我的真实陈述。

Zee Ah Kwei, aged 42 years, native of Tsingkong, Married,
residing at 18/120 Ningpo Road.
I have been employed as C.P.W. 275.
Between 2p.m. and 10p.m. on the 17-6-39 I was detailed for
duty in the 3rd sub-alleyway of Lane 120 Ningpo Road.
At about 8.50p.m. same date, I heard the sound of pistol
shots. I immediately drew my pistol and ran towards the mouth
of the alleyway but on arrival, I could not find anyone who was
responsible for the shooting. All what I could see was that

Meanwhile a party of Police attended the scene. The above is

谢阿贵（Zee Ah Kwei），42岁，青浦人，已婚，居住在宁波路120号18室。
我受雇为华捕警号 275。
1939年6月17日下午2时至晚上10时之间，我被派往宁波路120弄的第三条支弄执行勤务。
同日约晚上8时50分，我听到枪声。我立即拔出手枪跑向巷口，但到达时，我找不到任何对枪击负责的人。我所看到的只是有人向宁波路130号《导报》馆投掷了一枚手榴弹，但未爆炸。
同时，一队警察抵达现场。以上是我的真实陈述。

page_data.en:
Chu Nyoh Sz.

Ningpo
Central Stn.    17-6-39.    translated
                              /--------    Clerk Fan

    Chu Nyoh Sz, aged 47 years, native of Ningpo, widow,
working as a laundry woman by profession, residing at No. 16
Zee Ka Hwa Yuen, Tsepoo Road.
    At about 8p.m. on the 17-6-39, I left home and proceeded
to the Morning Leader Newspaper Office, 130 Ningpo Road with
intent to sew a quilt for the teaboy in the employ of the above
newspaper office. Whilst I was sewing the quilt on a desk in the
office I suddenly heard the sound "Ping Ping" and someone
shouted "Pistol shots". I therefore took to my heels and
hastily ascended the staircase and, upon reaching the 1st floor,
I intended to climb out of the window and conceal myself there,
but unfortunately I fell through the corrugated iron shed which
resulted in my sustaining injuries on my head and hip.
    The above is my true statement.

朱若思（Chu Nyoh Sz）。

宁波
中央巡捕房    1939年6月17日。    翻译
                              /--------    书记员 Fan

    朱若思（Chu Nyoh Sz），47岁，宁波人，寡妇，职业为洗衣妇，居住在乍浦路张家花园16号。
    1939年6月17日晚约8时，我离开家，前往宁波路130号《导报》馆，打算为该报馆雇佣的茶役缝制一床棉被。当我在办公室的一张桌子上缝制棉被时，我突然听到“乒乒乓乓”的声音，有人喊道“枪声”。于是我拔腿就跑，匆忙登上楼梯，到达一楼时，我本想爬出窗户躲藏在那里，但不幸的是，我跌穿了波纹铁皮棚顶，导致头部和臀部受伤。
    以上是我的真实陈述。

probably cause the newspaper to cease publication for about
one week. However, Mr.Shiotani stated that a half day was
sufficient to replace all lead types into the proper sequence.
Mr.Shiotani urged Au to think of some other better device,and
Au then left the office.

After the lapse of about one week,Au again attended the
office and Mr.Shiotani asked him if he had arranged some plan.
As Au did not have any suggestion to offer along this line,
Mr.Shiotani suggested that the art of incendiarism be adopted,
and asked him if he could find a 'brave man'. To this Au
replied in the affirmative. Mr.Shiotani stated that for the
purpose of arson a tin fully packed with chemical powder
could start a conflagration within 30 minutes. He went on to
say that a sum of five or six hundred dollars would be paid
to the courageous man who performed the act,no mention being
made of Au's remuneration. As Au insisted on an advance
payment. Mr. Shiotani agreed upon the payment of $200.00 in
advance. Au then promised to consider the matter, stating he
he an intimate friend eligible for this mission.

At about 2 p.m.on the 6-8-38 Au telephoned to me stating
that he had obtained the consent of his friend named Shui
(actually the witness Tseng Ping Yee). I in turn informed Mr.
Shiotani. The latter instructed me to request Au to bring
his friend named Shui to the office, but this request was
refused. However, Au stated that he had booked a room in the
Oriental Hotel,Nanking Road,which I was expected to visit for
further conversation. Mr.Shiotani on being informed of the
page_data.zh:
-2-

可能导致该报停刊约一周。然而，盐谷先生（Mr. Shiotani）表示，半天时间足以将所有铅字重新排好序。
盐谷先生敦促欧某（Au）想些其他更好的办法，随后欧某离开了办公室。

大约一周后，欧某再次来到办公室，盐谷先生问他是否安排了什么计划。由于欧某在这方面提不出任何建议，盐谷先生建议采用纵火术，并问他是否能找到一个“勇敢的人”。对此，欧某给予了肯定答复。盐谷先生称，为了纵火目的，一个装满化学粉末的锡罐可以在30分钟内引发大火。他接着说，将支付五百或六百美元给执行此行动的勇敢者，未提及欧某的报酬。由于欧某坚持要求预付款，盐谷先生同意预付200.00美元。欧某随后答应考虑此事，称他有一位适合执行此任务的亲密朋友。

1938年8月6日下午2点左右，欧某打电话给我，称已获得其朋友水某（Shui）（实为证人曾平义 Tseng Ping Yee）的同意。我随即告知盐谷先生。后者指示我要求欧某带其朋友水某来办公室，但这一要求被拒绝。然而，欧某称他在南京路东方饭店（Oriental Hotel）预订了一个房间，期望我去那里进行进一步交谈。盐谷先生在得知

page_data.en:
-3-

proposed visit stated he would accompany me to the said hotel.
At about 4.30p.m. same date he and I proceeded to the aforesaid
hotel where we met Au and Shui. Mr. Shiotani asked Shui if he
was an employee of the University Press, and Shui stated that he
was employed as a foreman in that newspaper company. Mr. Shiotani
then asked the following questions concerning the topography
of the said Co.:- (1) The situation of front and rear doors
of the Co., (2) The position of the alleyway in which the rear
door is situated, (3) The number of workers on the premises, and
(4) The distance of the University Press premises from other
neighbouring buildings.

Mr. Shiotani also asked Shui to draw a sketch of the
inside view of the newspaper building, and he reiterated
his plan of arson to Shui. Before Shui gave any consent of
the mission, Mr. Shiotani insisted that if Shui proposed to
accept the work he should first draw a rough plan of the
building on a sheet of white paper, and also submit two
copies of his photograph.

After two or three days Au Wei Sung telephoned to me,
and stated that the plan would be materialized after the
advent of 13/8/38.

At about 6 p.m. on the 27/8/38 Au telephoned to me
requesting my appearance at the Wu Koong Hotel, Foochow Rd.,
but I did not visit that address.

At about 3p.m. 28/8/38 Au Wei Sung again phoned up
requesting me to visit Room 536, the Oriental Hotel, Nanking
Rd. After informing Mr. Shiotani of the above, I proceeded
page_data.zh:
-3-

提议的访问中，他表示将陪同我前往上述旅馆。同日下午约4时30分，他与我一同前往前述旅馆，在那里我们会见了Au和Shui。盐谷先生（Mr. Shiotani）询问Shui是否为商务印书馆的雇员，Shui称他在该报馆受雇担任领班。随后，盐谷先生就该公司地形情况提出了以下问题：(1) 公司前后门的位置；(2) 后门所在弄堂的位置；(3) 厂区内工人的数量；以及 (4) 商务印书馆厂区与周边其他建筑物的距离。

盐谷先生还要求Shui绘制报馆内部视图的草图，并向Shui重申了他的纵火计划。在Shui同意执行该任务之前，盐谷先生坚持要求，如果Shui打算接受这项工作，他必须首先在一张白纸上绘制该建筑物的粗略平面图，并提交两张他的照片。

两三天后，Au Wei Sung（音译）给我打电话，表示该计划将在1938年8月13日之后实施。

1938年8月27日下午约6时，Au打电话给我，要求我前往福州路吴宫旅馆（Wu Koong Hotel），但我未前往该地址。

1938年8月28日下午约3时，Au Wei Sung（音译）再次来电，要求我前往南京路东方饭店（Oriental Hotel）536号房间。我将上述情况告知盐谷先生后，便动身

page_data.en:
-4-
to the said hotel at about 4p.m. same date.However,upon arrival
I was put under arrest by the detectives.
Signed.
J. Ross.
29/5/38.
